faq.q: Do I need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2041?
faq.a: No, not if you book a yacht with a licensed skipper, which is how we operate. All our boats include a professional skipper, so you can relax and enjoy the coast. The 2041 rules mainly affect self-drive rentals without a skipper, where a licence is required for boats over 15 metres.

faq.q: What licence do I need to drive a boat in Spain in 2041?
faq.a: For recreational boating in Spain, you need the 'Licencia de Navegación' for boats up to 6 metres or 15 kW. For larger vessels up to 15 metres, the 'Patrón de Navegación Básica' (PNB) is required. The 2041 update extends the PNB requirement to self-drive boats over 15 metres, but this doesn't affect skipper-led charters.

faq.q: Can I charter a yacht without a licence in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Most of our charters are skipper-inclusive, meaning you don't need any licence. You just step aboard, and the skipper handles navigation. This applies to all our boats, from the 8-metre Dubhe to the 29-metre Ferretti 94.

faq.q: Are there any age restrictions for chartering a yacht in Marbella?
faq.a: You must be at least 18 years old to book a charter. There's no upper age limit, but for safety, we recommend guests be reasonably mobile. Children are welcome on most boats; life jackets are provided for all sizes.

faq.q: What's included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). So the price you see is the price you pay – no hidden extras.

faq.q: Do I need to show any documents before boarding?
faq.a: You'll need a valid ID or passport for the booking. If you've booked a self-drive charter (not our standard), you'd need to present your Spanish or international boating licence. For skipper-led charters, no boating documents are required.

faq.q: What about international licences – are they valid in Spain?
faq.a: Yes, if you hold a valid recreational boating licence from your home country, it's generally recognised in Spain, especially if it's an International Certificate of Competence (ICC). However, since our charters include a skipper, you won't need to present it.

data.body_html:
Planning a yacht charter in Marbella for 2041? The rules have been updated, and you might be wondering if you need a licence. The short answer: for most charters, no – because you're not driving the boat. But there are new regulations for self-drive hire. Here's what you need to know, with concrete numbers and no fluff.

What Changed in 2041?

Spain's maritime authority updated the recreational boating regulations, effective January 2041. The key change: for self-drive boat rentals, a licence is now mandatory for vessels over 15 metres in length (previously 24 metres). This means if you plan to captain a larger yacht yourself, you'll need a 'Patrón de Yate' or equivalent. However, this rule only applies to bareboat charters without a skipper. Our charters always include a licensed skipper, so you're unaffected.

Do You Need a Licence for a Skippered Charter?

No. When you book a yacht with a skipper, the skipper holds the required qualifications. You're a guest, not the captain. This applies to all our boats, from the compact Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) to the superyacht Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). You just relax, swim, and enjoy the Costa del Sol. We handle the paperwork.

Boat Sizes and Licence Thresholds

For context, here's how the 2041 rules break down by boat length:

  • Up to 6m: 'Licencia de Navegación' (basic, no exam for some cases).
  • 6m to 15m: 'Patrón de Navegación Básica' (PNB) – required for self-drive.
  • Over 15m: 'Patrón de Yate' – now required for self-drive as of 2041.

Our fleet ranges from 6.4m (Mariah SX21) to 29m (Ferretti 94). But since every charter includes a skipper, these thresholds never apply to you.

What About Self-Drive Rentals?

We don't offer bareboat charters – our boats come with a skipper for your safety and convenience. If you're set on driving yourself, you'd need to look elsewhere, but you'd need a valid licence and insurance. For most visitors, a skipper-led charter is simpler and more relaxing, especially if you're unfamiliar with local waters.

Practical Tips for 2041 Charters

  • Book early – summer weekends sell out.
  • Bring a valid ID or passport for the manifest.
  • No boating licence needed – just show up.
  • Ask about custom routes: Cabopino, Estepona, or Sotogrande.
  • For specific licence questions, WhatsApp us – we'll clarify.

Popular Routes and Destinations

From Puerto Banús, you can cruise to Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or along the Golden Mile. For a longer trip, head to Estepona or even Sotogrande. Your skipper knows the best anchorages for swimming and dining. The 2041 rules don't affect these routes – they're all within coastal navigation limits.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2041?

No, not if you book a yacht with a licensed skipper, which is how we operate. All our boats include a professional skipper, so you can relax and enjoy the coast. The 2041 rules mainly affect self-drive rentals without a skipper, where a licence is required for boats over 15 metres.

What licence do I need to drive a boat in Spain in 2041?

For recreational boating in Spain, you need the 'Licencia de Navegación' for boats up to 6 metres or 15 kW. For larger vessels up to 15 metres, the 'Patrón de Navegación Básica' (PNB) is required. The 2041 update extends the PNB requirement to self-drive boats over 15 metres, but this doesn't affect skipper-led charters.

Can I charter a yacht without a licence in Marbella?

Yes, absolutely. Most of our charters are skipper-inclusive, meaning you don't need any licence. You just step aboard, and the skipper handles navigation. This applies to all our boats, from the 8-metre Dubhe to the 29-metre Ferretti 94.

Are there any age restrictions for chartering a yacht in Marbella?

You must be at least 18 years old to book a charter. There's no upper age limit, but for safety, we recommend guests be reasonably mobile. Children are welcome on most boats; life jackets are provided for all sizes.

What's included in the charter price?

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). So the price you see is the price you pay – no hidden extras.

Do I need to show any documents before boarding?

You'll need a valid ID or passport for the booking. If you've booked a self-drive charter (not our standard), you'd need to present your Spanish or international boating licence. For skipper-led charters, no boating documents are required.

What about international licences – are they valid in Spain?

Yes, if you hold a valid recreational boating licence from your home country, it's generally recognised in Spain, especially if it's an International Certificate of Competence (ICC). However, since our charters include a skipper, you won't need to present it.
